title.zh: 卷五十四 雜傳第四十二: 序言 馮道 李琪 鄭玨 李愚 盧導 司空頲
title.en: Volume 54 Miscellaneous Biographies 34: Xu Yan, Feng Dao, Li Qi, Zheng Jue, Li Yu, Lu Dao, Si Kongting
title.raw: 卷五十四 雜傳第四十二: 序言 馮道 李琪 鄭玨 李愚 盧導 司空頲 Volume 54 Miscellaneous Biographies 34: Xu Yan, Feng Dao, Li Qi, Zheng Jue, Li Yu, Lu Dao, Si Kongting

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「禮義廉恥，國之四維；

translations.literal: The Classic of History says: "Ritual, righteousness, integrity, and shame are the four bonds of a state;
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say: "Ritual, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame are the four pillars of the state;

sentences.zh: 四維不張，國乃滅亡。

translations.literal: if the four bonds are not extended, the state will perish."
translations.idiomatic: if these four pillars are not upheld, the state will be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 」善乎，管生之能言也！

translations.literal: How well said—Master Guan's power of expression!
translations.idiomatic: Well said indeed—how aptly Master Guan put it!

sentences.zh: 禮義，治人之大法；

translations.literal: Ritual and righteousness are the great laws for governing people;
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and righteousness are the great principles by which men are governed;

sentences.zh: 廉恥，立人之大節。

translations.literal: integrity and shame are the great standards for establishing a person.
translations.idiomatic: integrity and shame are the great standards by which a person stands upright.

sentences.zh: 蓋不廉，則無所不取；

translations.literal: For if one lacks integrity, there is nothing he will not seize;
translations.idiomatic: Without integrity, a man will seize anything;

sentences.zh: 不恥，則無所不為。

translations.literal: if one lacks shame, there is nothing he will not do.
translations.idiomatic: without shame, he will stoop to anything.

sentences.zh: 人而如此，則禍亂敗亡，亦無所不至，況為大臣而無所不取，無所不為，則天下其有不亂，國家其有不亡者乎！

translations.literal: When a man is like this, calamity, disorder, ruin, and destruction know no limit; how much more when a great minister will seize anything and do anything—can the realm fail to fall into chaos, or the state fail to perish!
translations.idiomatic: When ordinary men behave this way, disaster and ruin follow without limit; when great ministers seize anything and stoop to anything, how can the realm remain at peace or the state escape destruction?

sentences.zh: 予讀馮道《長樂老敘》，見其自述以為榮，其可謂無廉恥者矣，則天下國家可從而知也。

translations.literal: When I read Feng Dao's "Account of the Old Man of Everlasting Joy," I saw that he took pride in his own account of himself; one may say he had no integrity or shame, and from this the realm and the state may be understood.
translations.idiomatic: When I read Feng Dao's Account of the Old Man of Everlasting Joy and saw him boast of his own career, I knew him for a man utterly devoid of integrity and shame—and from that one may infer the fate of realm and state.

sentences.zh: 予於五代，得全節之士三，死事之臣十有五，而怪士之被服儒者以學古自名，而享人之祿、任人之國者多矣，然使忠義之節，獨出於武夫戰卒，豈於儒者果無其人哉？

translations.literal: In the Five Dynasties I found three men who preserved their integrity whole and fifteen ministers who died for their cause; yet I marvel that many who wore the robes of Confucians and styled themselves students of antiquity enjoyed others' stipends and bore charge of others' states—yet loyalty and righteousness should appear only among military men and common soldiers; can it be that among Confucians there truly were no such men?
translations.idiomatic: In the Five Dynasties I could name only three men who kept their integrity intact and fifteen who died for their sovereign; yet countless men in Confucian garb who called themselves students of antiquity drew salaries and governed states—while loyalty and righteousness seemed to belong to soldiers alone. Were there truly no such men among the scholars?

sentences.zh: 豈非高節之士惡時之亂，薄其世而不肯出歟？

translations.literal: Was it not that men of lofty integrity detested the disorder of the age, held their times in contempt, and refused to come forth?
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps men of lofty principle despised the chaos of the age, held the times in contempt, and refused to serve?

sentences.zh: 抑君天下者不足顧，而莫能致之歟？

translations.literal: Or was it that those who ruled all under Heaven were unworthy of regard and could not summon them forth?
translations.idiomatic: Or were the rulers themselves unworthy of such men, and unable to draw them from retirement?

sentences.zh: 孔子以謂：「十室之邑，必有忠信。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "In a hamlet of ten households there must be loyalty and trustworthiness."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "Even in a hamlet of ten households, there are sure to be men of loyalty and good faith."

sentences.zh: 」豈虛言也哉！

translations.literal: Was this empty talk!
translations.idiomatic: His words were no idle boast!

sentences.zh: 予嘗得五代時小說一篇，載王凝妻李氏事，以一婦人猶能如此，則知世固嘗有其人而不得見也。

translations.literal: I once obtained a tale from the Five Dynasties that records the affair of Wang Ning's wife, Lady Li; that even a woman could act thus shows that the age surely had such people who went unseen.
translations.idiomatic: I once came upon a Five Dynasties tale about Wang Ning's wife, Lady Li; that even a woman could act so nobly proves that such people existed in the world, though we never saw them.

sentences.zh: 凝家青、齊之間，為虢州司戶參軍，以疾卒於官。

translations.literal: Ning's family was from between Qing and Qi; he served as registrar of households in Guo Prefecture and died of illness in office.
translations.idiomatic: Ning's family came from the region between Qing and Qi. He served as registrar of households in Guo Prefecture and died of illness while in office.

sentences.zh: 凝家素貧，一子尚幼，李氏攜其子，負其遺骸以歸。

translations.literal: The Ning household had long been poor; one son was still young. Lady Li took her child and carried her husband's remains home.
translations.idiomatic: The Ning family had always been poor. Their son was still a child. Lady Li took the boy on her back and bore her husband's remains home.

sentences.zh: 東過開封，止旅舍，旅舍主人見其婦人獨攜一子而疑之，不許其宿。

translations.literal: Traveling east past Kaifeng, she stopped at an inn; the innkeeper, seeing a woman traveling alone with one child, grew suspicious and would not let her stay.
translations.idiomatic: Passing east through Kaifeng, she stopped at an inn. The innkeeper, seeing a woman traveling alone with a small child, suspected her and refused her lodging.

sentences.zh: 李氏顧天已暮，不肯去，主人牽其臂而出之。

translations.literal: Lady Li saw that night had come and would not leave; the innkeeper seized her arm and dragged her out.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li saw that night was falling and would not go. The innkeeper seized her by the arm and thrust her outside.

sentences.zh: 李氏仰天長慟曰：「我為婦人，不能守節，而此手為人執邪？

translations.literal: Lady Li looked up to heaven and wailed long: "I am a woman who could not keep her chastity—and shall this hand be held by another man?"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li looked up to heaven and wailed: "I am a woman who could not keep her chastity intact—shall this hand be grasped by a stranger?"

sentences.zh: 不可以一手並汙吾身！

translations.literal: I cannot let one hand defile my whole person!
translations.idiomatic: I cannot let a single hand defile my whole body!"

sentences.zh: 」即引斧自斷其臂。

translations.literal: She at once took an axe and cut off her own arm.
translations.idiomatic: She seized an axe and cut off her own arm.

sentences.zh: 路人見者，環聚而嗟之，或為彈指，或為之泣下。

translations.literal: Passersby who saw it gathered in a ring and sighed; some snapped their fingers in wonder, some wept.
translations.idiomatic: Passersby gathered round and sighed; some snapped their fingers in awe, others wept.

sentences.zh: 開封尹聞之，白其事於朝，官為賜藥封瘡，厚恤李氏，而笞其主人者。

translations.literal: The prefect of Kaifeng heard of it, reported the matter to court, and officials provided medicine to dress the wound, gave Lady Li generous relief, and had the innkeeper flogged.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Kaifeng reported the affair to court. Officials sent medicine to dress her wound, gave Lady Li generous relief, and had the innkeeper flogged.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，士不自愛其身而忍恥以偷生者，聞李氏之風，宜少知愧哉！

translations.literal: Alas! Scholars who do not cherish their own persons but endure shame to cling to life—hearing Lady Li's example, ought they not feel some shame!
translations.idiomatic: Alas! Scholars who do not value their own honor but endure shame merely to cling to life—hearing of Lady Li, ought they not feel at least a little ashamed?

sentences.zh: 馮道，字可道，瀛州景城人也。

translations.literal: Feng Dao, courtesy name Kedao, was a man of Jingcheng in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao, courtesy name Kedao, was a native of Jingcheng in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 事劉守光為參軍，守光敗，去事宦者張承業。

translations.literal: He served Liu Shouguang as aide; when Shouguang was defeated, he left to serve the eunuch Zhang Chengye.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liu Shouguang as military aide. When Shouguang fell, he went to serve the eunuch Zhang Chengye.

sentences.zh: 承業監河東軍，以為巡官，以其文學薦之晉王，為河東節度掌書記。

translations.literal: Chengye supervised the Hedong army and made him touring officer; because of his literary talent he recommended him to the Prince of Jin, and he became secretary to the Hedong military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye, who supervised the Hedong army, appointed him touring officer and, impressed by his literary talent, recommended him to the Prince of Jin. Feng Dao became secretary to the Hedong military governor.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，拜戶部侍郎，充翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne, he was appointed vice minister of revenue and made Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong ascended the throne, Feng Dao was appointed vice minister of revenue and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 道為人，能自刻苦為儉約。

translations.literal: Dao as a man could impose hardship on himself and practice frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao was a man who could impose hardship on himself and lived frugally.

sentences.zh: 當晉與梁夾河而軍，道居軍中，為一茅庵，不設床席，臥一束芻而已。

translations.literal: When Jin and Liang faced each other across the Yellow River with their armies, Dao lived in camp in a thatched hut, set out no bed or mat, and slept on a bundle of straw alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin and Liang faced each other across the Yellow River, Feng Dao lived in camp in a thatched hut with no bed or mat, sleeping on a bundle of straw.

sentences.zh: 所得俸祿，與仆廝同器飲食，意恬如也。

translations.literal: His salary he ate from the same vessel as his servants, content in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He shared his salary food from the same bowl as his servants and seemed perfectly content.

sentences.zh: 諸將有掠得人之美女者以遺道，道不能卻，置之別室，訪其主而還之。

translations.literal: When generals plundered beautiful women and presented them to Dao, he could not refuse outright; he placed them in a separate room, sought out their owners, and returned them.
translations.idiomatic: When generals seized beautiful women and offered them to him, he could not refuse outright; he housed them separately, found their rightful owners, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 其解學士居父喪於景城，遇歲饑，悉出所有以赒鄉里，而退耕於野，躬自負薪。

translations.literal: When he left his post as academician to observe mourning for his father in Jingcheng, a famine year came; he gave all he had to relieve the countryside, withdrew to farm in the wilds, and carried firewood on his own back.
translations.idiomatic: When he left his academician post to mourn his father in Jingcheng, famine struck. He gave away everything he owned to aid the countryside, then withdrew to farm in the fields and carried firewood on his own back.

sentences.zh: 有荒其田不耕者與力不能耕者，道夜往，潛為之耕。

translations.literal: For those who let their fields lie fallow and those who lacked strength to plow, Dao went by night and secretly plowed for them.
translations.idiomatic: For neighbors who left fields untilled or lacked strength to plow, he went by night and secretly tilled their land.

sentences.zh: 其人後來愧謝，道殊不以為德。

translations.literal: When they later came ashamed to thank him, Dao did not regard it as a favor at all.
translations.idiomatic: When they later came to thank him in shame, he gave the matter no thought.

sentences.zh: 服除，復召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was again summoned as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was recalled as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 行至汴州，遇趙在禮作亂，明宗自魏擁兵還，犯京師。

translations.literal: Reaching Bian Prefecture, he encountered Zhao Zaili's rebellion; Emperor Mingzong returned from Wei at the head of troops and marched on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the road to Bian Prefecture he encountered Zhao Zaili's rebellion. Emperor Mingzong marched from Wei at the head of an army against the capital.

sentences.zh: 孔循勸道少留以待，道曰：「吾奉詔赴闕，豈可自留！

translations.literal: Kong Xun urged Dao to stay a while and wait; Dao said: "I have received orders to proceed to court—how can I remain of my own accord!"
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xun urged him to wait awhile. Feng Dao said: "I have received orders to proceed to court—how can I stay behind on my own?"

sentences.zh: 」乃疾趨至京師。

translations.literal: He then hurried on to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on at once to the capital.

sentences.zh: 莊宗遇弒，明宗即位，雅知道所為，問安重誨曰：「先帝時馮道何在？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong met assassination; Mingzong took the throne and had long known Dao's conduct. He asked An Chonghui: "Where was Feng Dao in the former emperor's time?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was assassinated and Mingzong took the throne. Mingzong had long admired Feng Dao's conduct and asked An Chonghui: "Where was Feng Dao during the late emperor's reign?"

sentences.zh: 」重誨曰：「為學士也。

translations.literal: Chonghui said: "He was academician."
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui answered: "He was Hanlin academician."

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「吾素知之，此真吾宰相也。

translations.literal: Mingzong said: "I have long known him—this is truly my chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong said: "I have known him for years—this is truly the man for my chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」拜道端明殿學士，遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Dao was appointed academician of the Hall of Duanming and promoted to vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao was appointed academician of the Hall of Duanming and promoted to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent director of the Secretariat with the Grand Councilor title.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 天成、長興之間，歲屢豐熟，中國無事。

translations.literal: Between the Tiancheng and Changxing reigns harvests were repeatedly abundant and the central realm was at peace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng and Changxing reigns harvests were repeatedly abundant and the heartland knew peace.

sentences.zh: 道嘗戒明宗曰：「臣為河東掌書記時，奉使中山，過井陘之險，懼馬蹶失，不敢怠於銜轡；

translations.literal: Dao once admonished Mingzong: "When I was secretary in Hedong I went on mission to Zhongshan and passed the peril of Jingxing Pass; fearing the horse might stumble, I did not dare slacken the bridle;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao once cautioned Mingzong: "When I was secretary in Hedong I traveled to Zhongshan and crossed the perilous Jingxing Pass. Fearing my horse might stumble, I never slackened the reins;

sentences.zh: 及至平地，謂無足慮，遽跌而傷。

translations.literal: when I reached level ground I thought there was nothing to worry about, and suddenly fell and was injured."
translations.idiomatic: but once I reached level ground I thought myself safe—and promptly fell and was hurt."

sentences.zh: 凡蹈危者慮深而獲全，居安者患生於所忽，此人情之常也。

translations.literal: In general those who tread danger think deeply and come through whole; those who dwell in ease find trouble born of what they neglect—such is the constant way of human feeling."
translations.idiomatic: Those who face danger think deeply and survive; those who live at ease invite disaster through carelessness. That is human nature."

sentences.zh: 」明宗問曰：「天下雖豐，百姓濟否？

translations.literal: Mingzong asked: "Though the realm is abundant, are the common people provided for?"
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong asked: "The realm is rich, but are the people truly provided for?"

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「谷貴餓農，谷賤傷農。

translations.literal: Dao said: "When grain is dear the farmers starve; when grain is cheap the farmers are hurt."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao answered: "When grain is dear the farmers starve; when grain is cheap the farmers suffer."

sentences.zh: 」因誦文士聶夷中《田家詩》，其言近而易曉。

translations.literal: He then recited the literary man Nie Yizhong's "Farmhouse Poem," whose words were close at hand and easy to understand.
translations.idiomatic: He then recited Nie Yizhong's Farmhouse Poem, whose words were plain and easy to grasp.

sentences.zh: 明宗顧左右錄其詩，常以自誦。

translations.literal: Mingzong had those beside him copy the poem and often recited it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong had attendants copy the poem and often recited it himself.

sentences.zh: 水運軍將於臨河縣得一玉杯，有文曰「傳國寶萬歲杯」，明宗甚愛之，以示道，道曰：「此前世有形之寶爾，王者固有無形之寶也。

translations.literal: A transport officer at Linhe County obtained a jade cup inscribed "Transmission-of-the-Realm Treasure, Cup of Ten Thousand Years"; Mingzong loved it greatly and showed it to Dao. Dao said: "This is only a treasure with form from former ages; kings also have treasures without form."
translations.idiomatic: A transport officer at Linhe County found a jade cup inscribed "Transmission-of-the-Realm Treasure, Cup of Ten Thousand Years." Mingzong treasured it and showed it to Feng Dao, who said: "This is only a tangible treasure of former ages. A true king possesses intangible treasures as well."

sentences.zh: 」明宗問之，道曰：「仁義者，帝王之寶也。

translations.literal: Mingzong asked what they were; Dao said: "Benevolence and righteousness are the treasures of emperors and kings."
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong asked what those were. Feng Dao said: "Benevolence and righteousness are the emperor's true treasures."

sentences.zh: 故曰：『大寶曰位，何以守位曰仁。

translations.literal: Thus it is said: 'The great treasure is the throne; by what is the throne kept? By benevolence.'"
translations.idiomatic: As the classic says: 'The great treasure is the throne; how is the throne kept? By benevolence.'"

sentences.zh: 』」明宗武君，不曉其言，道已去，召侍臣講說其義，嘉納之。

translations.literal: Mingzong was a martial ruler and did not understand his words; after Dao had left, he summoned attendants to explain the meaning and praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was a martial man and did not grasp the point. After Feng Dao left, he summoned his attendants to explain the passage and praised the advice warmly.

sentences.zh: 道相明宗十餘年，明宗崩，相湣帝。

translations.literal: Dao served as chief minister to Mingzong for more than ten years; when Mingzong died he served Emperor Min.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao served as chief minister to Mingzong for more than ten years. When Mingzong died, he served Emperor Min.

sentences.zh: 潞王反於鳳翔，湣帝出奔衛州，道率百官迎潞王入，是為廢帝，遂相之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu rebelled at Fengxiang; Emperor Min fled to Weizhou. Dao led the hundred officials to welcome the Prince of Lu into the capital—he became Emperor Fei—and then served him as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu rebelled at Fengxiang. Emperor Min fled to Weizhou. Feng Dao led the officials to welcome the prince into the capital as Emperor Fei and again became his chief minister.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，湣帝猶在衛州，後三日，湣帝始遇弒崩。

translations.literal: When Emperor Fei took the throne, Emperor Min was still at Weizhou; three days later Emperor Min was assassinated and died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Fei took the throne while Emperor Min was still at Weizhou. Three days later Min was assassinated.

sentences.zh: 已而廢帝出道為同州節度使，逾年，拜司空。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Fei sent Dao out as military governor of Tong Prefecture; after more than a year he was appointed grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Emperor Fei sent Feng Dao out as military governor of Tong Prefecture. A year later he was appointed grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 晉滅唐，道又事晉，晉高祖拜道守司空、同中書門下平章事，加司徒，兼侍中，封魯國公。

translations.literal: Jin destroyed Tang; Dao again served Jin. Jin Gaozu appointed Dao to hold the post of grand marshal and concurrent Grand Councilor, added grand mentor, made him concurrent palace attendant, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin destroyed Tang, Feng Dao served Jin. Jin Gaozu appointed him grand marshal and Grand Councilor, then grand mentor and palace attendant, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，道相出帝，加太尉，封燕國公，罷為匡國軍節度使，徙鎮威勝。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, Dao served as chief minister to Emperor Chu, was promoted to grand commandant, enfeoffed as Duke of Yan, removed as military governor of the Kuangguo army, and transferred to Weisheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu died, Feng Dao served Emperor Chu as chief minister, was promoted to grand commandant and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan, then dismissed as military governor of Kuangguo and transferred to Weisheng.

sentences.zh: 契丹滅晉，道又事契丹，朝耶律德光於京師。

translations.literal: The Khitan destroyed Jin; Dao again served the Khitan and attended on Yelü Deguang at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan destroyed Jin. Feng Dao served them as well and presented himself to Yelü Deguang at the capital.

sentences.zh: 德光責道事晉無狀，道不能對。

translations.literal: Deguang reproached Dao for serving Jin disgracefully; Dao could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang reproached him for shamefully serving Jin. Feng Dao had no answer.

sentences.zh: 又問曰：「何以來朝？

translations.literal: He asked again: "Why have you come to court?"
translations.idiomatic: Deguang asked again: "Why have you come to court?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「無城無兵，安敢不來。

translations.literal: He answered: "Without walls or troops, how would I dare not come?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Without walls or troops, how could I dare stay away?"

sentences.zh: 」德光誚之曰：「爾是何等老子？

translations.literal: Deguang mocked him: "What sort of old fellow are you?"
translations.idiomatic: Deguang mocked him: "What sort of old fool are you?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「無才無德癡頑老子。

translations.literal: He answered: "A witless, virtueless, stupid and stubborn old fellow."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "A witless, virtueless, stubborn old fool."

sentences.zh: 」德光喜，以道為太傅。

translations.literal: Deguang was pleased and made Dao grand preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang was amused and appointed him grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 德光北歸，從至常山。

translations.literal: When Deguang returned north, Dao followed him to Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Deguang marched north, Feng Dao accompanied him as far as Changshan.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖立，乃歸漢，以太師奉朝請。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu was established, he then returned to Han and attended court as grand preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Gaozu was established, he returned to Han and attended court as grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 周滅漢，道又事周，周太祖拜道太師，兼中書令。

translations.literal: Zhou destroyed Han; Dao again served Zhou. Zhou Taizu appointed Dao grand preceptor and concurrent director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou destroyed Han, Feng Dao served Zhou. Zhou Taizu appointed him grand preceptor and director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 道少能矯行以取稱於世，及為大臣，尤務持重以鎮物，事四姓十君，益以舊德自處。

translations.literal: In youth Dao could discipline his conduct to win praise in the world; when he became a great minister he especially strove for weight and gravity to steady others. Serving four surnames and ten rulers, he all the more held himself by old virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he could discipline his conduct to win praise; as a great minister he cultivated weight and gravity to steady others. Having served four dynasties and ten sovereigns, he leaned ever more on his reputation as an elder statesman.

sentences.zh: 然當世之士無賢愚皆仰道為元老，而喜為之稱譽。

translations.literal: Yet men of the age, wise and foolish alike, looked up to Dao as an elder statesman and delighted to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet men of the age, wise and foolish alike, revered him as a patriarch of the court and delighted in praising him.

sentences.zh: 耶律德光嘗問道曰：「天下百姓如何救得？

translations.literal: Yelü Deguang once asked Dao: "How can the common people of the realm be saved?"
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Deguang once asked him: "How can the people of the realm be saved?"

sentences.zh: 」道為俳語以對曰：「此時佛出救不得，惟皇帝救得。

translations.literal: Dao answered in comic verse: "At this time not even the Buddha coming forth could save them—only the emperor can save them."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao answered in a jesting rhyme: "At this hour not even the Buddha could save them—only Your Majesty can."

sentences.zh: 」人皆以謂契丹不夷滅中國之人者，賴道一言之善也。

translations.literal: People all said that the Khitan did not exterminate the people of China thanks to the goodness of this one remark by Dao.
translations.idiomatic: People said the Khitan spared the Chinese population thanks to this one apt remark.

sentences.zh: 周兵反，犯京師，隱帝已崩，太祖謂漢大臣必行推戴，及見道，道殊無意。

translations.literal: Zhou troops rebelled and marched on the capital; Emperor Yin had already died. Taizu thought the Han ministers would surely press the investiture on him; when he saw Dao, Dao showed no intention at all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou troops rebelled and marched on the capital. Emperor Yin was already dead. Taizu expected the Han ministers to press the throne on him, but when he saw Feng Dao, Dao showed no such inclination.

sentences.zh: 太祖素拜道，因不得已拜之，道受之如平時，太祖意少沮，知漢未可代，遂陽立湘陰公赟為漢嗣，遣道迎赟於徐州。

translations.literal: Taizu had always bowed to Dao; now he bowed because he had no choice, and Dao received it as in ordinary times. Taizu's intent was somewhat dampened; knowing Han could not yet be replaced, he then pretended to install the Duke of Xiangyin, Yun, as Han heir and sent Dao to welcome Yun at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had always bowed to Feng Dao; now he bowed because he had no choice, and Dao received the bow as if nothing had changed. Taizu's ardor cooled. Seeing that Han could not yet be seized, he pretended to install the Duke of Xiangyin, Yun, as heir and sent Feng Dao to fetch him from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 赟未至，太祖將兵北至澶州，擁兵而反，遂代漢。

translations.literal: Before Yun arrived, Taizu led troops north to Dazhou, turned his army about, and replaced Han.
translations.idiomatic: Before Yun arrived, Taizu marched north to Dazhou, turned his army about, and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 議者謂道能沮太祖之謀而緩之，終不以晉、漢之亡責道也。

translations.literal: Commentators said Dao could dampen Taizu's scheme and slow it, and in the end they did not blame Dao for the fall of Jin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Feng Dao had slowed Taizu's plot and therefore bore no blame for the fall of Jin and Han.

sentences.zh: 然道視喪君亡國亦未嘗以屑意。

translations.literal: Yet Dao never troubled himself over the loss of rulers or the perishing of states.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Feng Dao never troubled himself over the loss of sovereigns or the ruin of states.

sentences.zh: 當是時，天下大亂，戎夷交侵，生民之命，急於倒懸，道方自號「長樂老」，著書數百言，陳己更事四姓及契丹所得階勛官爵以為榮。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was in great disorder; barbarians and aliens invaded in turn; the lives of the people hung as if inverted. Dao styled himself "Old Man of Everlasting Joy," composed a work of several hundred words, and set forth the ranks, honors, and offices he had received serving four surnames and the Khitan as glory.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the realm was in chaos, barbarians raided from every side, and the people's lives hung by a thread. Feng Dao styled himself the Old Man of Everlasting Joy and wrote several hundred words listing the ranks and offices he had received under four dynasties and the Khitan—and took pride in them.

sentences.zh: 自謂：「孝於家，忠於國，為子、為弟、為人臣、為師長、為夫、為父，有子、有孫。

translations.literal: He said of himself: "Filial in the family, loyal to the state; as son, as younger brother, as minister, as teacher and elder, as husband, as father—I have sons and grandsons."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote of himself: "Filial at home, loyal to the state; a son, a younger brother, a minister, a teacher, a husband, a father—with sons and grandsons."

sentences.zh: 時開一卷，時飲一杯，食味、別聲、被色，老安於當代，老而自樂，何樂如之？

translations.literal: At times I open a scroll, at times I drink a cup; savoring flavors, distinguishing sounds, enjoying colors—growing old at ease in the present age, old and self-content—what joy could surpass this?"
translations.idiomatic: Now and then I open a book, now and then I drink a cup; I savor food, sound, and color, grow old at ease in my own time, and find joy in old age—what greater pleasure could there be?"

sentences.zh: 」蓋其自述如此。

translations.literal: Such was his own account.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his own boast.

sentences.zh: 道前事九君，未嘗諫諍。

translations.literal: Before this Dao had served nine rulers and never once remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: In all his years serving nine rulers, Feng Dao had never once remonstrated with them.

sentences.zh: 世宗初即位，劉旻攻上黨，世宗曰：「劉旻少我，謂我新立而國有大喪，必不能出兵以戰。

translations.literal: When Shizong had just taken the throne, Liu Min attacked Shangdang. Shizong said: "Liu Min despises me, thinking I am newly enthroned and the state is in great mourning and surely cannot take the field to fight."
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong first took the throne, Liu Min attacked Shangdang. Shizong said: "Liu Min underestimates me. He thinks I am newly enthroned, the court is in mourning, and I cannot march to war."

sentences.zh: 且善用兵者出其不意，吾當自將擊之。

translations.literal: Moreover, those skilled in war strike where the enemy does not expect; I shall lead the attack myself."
translations.idiomatic: A skilled commander strikes where the enemy does not expect. I shall lead the army myself."

sentences.zh: 」道乃切諫，以為不可。

translations.literal: Dao then remonstrated earnestly, saying it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao remonstrated earnestly that he must not go.

sentences.zh: 世宗曰：「吾見唐太宗平定天下，敵無大小皆親征。

translations.literal: Shizong said: "I have seen how Emperor Taizong of Tang pacified the realm—enemies great and small, he led every campaign in person."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong said: "I have read how Tang Taizong pacified the realm—he led every campaign himself, against foes great and small."

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「陛下未可比唐太宗。

translations.literal: Dao said: "Your Majesty cannot be compared to Tang Taizong."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao said: "Your Majesty is no Tang Taizong."

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「劉旻烏合之眾，若遇我師，如山壓卵。

translations.literal: Shizong said: "Liu Min's rabble—if they meet my army, it will be like a mountain crushing an egg."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong said: "Liu Min's rabble will crumble before my army like a mountain crushing an egg."

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「陛下作得山定否？

translations.literal: Dao said: "Can Your Majesty be sure you are that mountain?"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao asked: "Can Your Majesty be sure you are that mountain?"

sentences.zh: 」世宗怒，起去，卒自將擊旻，果敗旻於高平。

translations.literal: Shizong was angry, rose and left, and in the end led the attack on Min himself; he indeed defeated Min at Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong rose in anger and left. He marched in person, defeated Liu Min at Gaoping, and proved Feng Dao wrong.

sentences.zh: 世宗取淮南，定三關，威武之振自高平始。

translations.literal: Shizong took Huainan and secured the Three Passes; the display of might and martial glory began from Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong seized Huainan and secured the Three Passes; his martial renown began at Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 其擊旻也，鄙道不以從行，以為太祖山陵使。

translations.literal: When he attacked Min he despised Dao and did not take him along, making him commissioner for Taizu's mausoleum instead.
translations.idiomatic: When he marched against Liu Min he scorned Feng Dao and left him behind as commissioner for Taizu's tomb.

sentences.zh: 葬畢而道卒，年七十三，謚曰文懿，追封瀛王。

translations.literal: When the burial was complete Dao died, aged seventy-three; his posthumous title was Wényì, and he was enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: When the burial was finished Feng Dao died, aged seventy-three. He was given the posthumous title Wényì and enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 道既卒，時人皆共稱嘆，以謂與孔子同壽，其喜為之稱譽蓋如此。

translations.literal: When Dao had died, men of the time all praised him together, saying he had lived as long as Confucius; such was their delight in praising him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, contemporaries praised him extravagantly, saying he had lived as long as Confucius—such was the world's fondness for praising him.

sentences.zh: 道有子吉。

translations.literal: Dao had a son named Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao had a son named Ji.

sentences.zh: 李琪

translations.literal: Li Qi
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi

sentences.zh: （兄掞）〉

translations.literal: (elder brother Shan)〉
translations.idiomatic: (elder brother Shan)〉

sentences.zh: 李琪，字臺秀，河西敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Li Qi, styled Taixiu, was a man of Dunhuang in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi, styled Taixiu, was from Dunhuang in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 其兄珽，唐末舉進士及第，為監察御史。

translations.literal: His elder brother Ting, at the end of Tang passed the jinshi examination, and served as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Li Ting passed the jinshi examination in the late Tang and served as Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，貧無以葬，乞食而後葬。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning for his mother, he was too poor to bury her and begged for food before he could do so.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered mourning for his mother, he was too poor to bury her and had to beg for food before he could afford the funeral.

sentences.zh: 珽饑臥廬中，聞者哀憐之。

translations.literal: Ting lay starving in his hut, and those who heard of it pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Ting lay starving in his hut, and all who heard of it pitied him.

sentences.zh: 服除，還拜御史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he returned to office as censor.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, he returned to office as censor.

sentences.zh: 荊南成汭辟掌書記。

translations.literal: Cheng Rui of Jingnan recruited him as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Rui of Jingnan recruited him as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 吳兵圍杜洪，梁太祖遣汭與馬殷等救洪。

translations.literal: Wu troops besieged Du Hong, and Emperor Taizu of Liang sent Rui with Ma Yin and others to rescue Hong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu troops besieged Du Hong, Emperor Taizu of Liang sent Cheng Rui with Ma Yin and others to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 汭以大舟載兵數萬，珽為汭謀曰：「今一舟容甲士千人，糗糧倍之，緩急不可動，若為敵人縻之，則武陵、武安必為公之後患。

translations.literal: Rui loaded tens of thousands of troops on great ships. Ting counseled Rui, saying: "Now one ship holds a thousand armored soldiers, and rations double that; in an emergency it cannot move. If the enemy ties you down, Wuling and Wu'an will surely become future troubles for you.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Rui loaded tens of thousands of troops onto great ships. Ting advised him: "Each ship holds a thousand armored soldiers and twice that in rations—it cannot maneuver quickly in a crisis. If the enemy pins you down, Wuling and Wu'an will become your lasting trouble.

sentences.zh: 不若以勁兵屯巴陵，壁不與戰，吳兵糧盡，則圍解矣。

translations.literal: Better to station crack troops at Baling, hold the walls and refuse battle; when the Wu troops' provisions are exhausted, the siege will be lifted."
translations.idiomatic: Better to station crack troops at Baling, hold the walls, and refuse battle. When the Wu army runs out of provisions, the siege will lift of itself."

sentences.zh: 」汭不聽，汭果敗，溺死。

translations.literal: Rui would not listen; Rui indeed was defeated and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Rui would not listen. He was defeated and drowned.

sentences.zh: 趙匡凝鎮襄陽，又辟掌書記。

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangning governed Xiangyang and again recruited him as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangning, military governor of Xiangyang, recruited him again as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 太祖破匡凝，得珽，喜曰：「此真書記也。

translations.literal: Taizu defeated Kuangning, obtained Ting, and said with delight: "This is a true secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu defeated Zhao Kuangning and took Ting into his service, he said with delight: "This is a secretary in the true sense.

sentences.zh: 」太祖即位，除考功員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, he appointed him Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, he appointed Ting Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 珽度太祖不欲先用故吏，固辭不拜，出知曹州。

translations.literal: Ting surmised that Taizu did not wish to employ former subordinates at once; he firmly declined the appointment and went out to govern Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ting guessed that Taizu did not wish to promote former subordinates right away, firmly declined the appointment, and went out to govern Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曹州素劇難理，前刺史十餘輩，皆坐廢，珽至，以治聞。

translations.literal: Cao Prefecture had always been notoriously hard to govern; more than ten previous prefects had all been dismissed for misconduct. When Ting arrived, he became known for good administration.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Prefecture was notoriously difficult to govern—more than ten previous prefects had been dismissed for misconduct. When Ting arrived, he earned a reputation for effective rule.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部郎中、崇政院直學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director in the Ministry of War and Academic Scholar of the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director in the Ministry of War and Academic Scholar of the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 許州馮行襲病，行襲有牙兵二千，皆故蔡卒，太祖懼為變。

translations.literal: Feng Xingxi of Xu Prefecture fell ill. Xingxi had two thousand guard troops, all former soldiers of Cai, and Taizu feared a mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xingxi of Xu Prefecture fell ill. He had two thousand guard troops, all veterans of Cai, and Taizu feared they might rebel.

sentences.zh: 行襲為人嚴酷，從事魏峻切諫，行襲怒，誣以贓下獄，欲誅之。

translations.literal: Xingxi was harsh by nature. His aide Wei Jun remonstrated sharply; Xingxi grew angry, falsely charged him with embezzlement, threw him in prison, and wished to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Xingxi was a harsh man. When his aide Wei Jun remonstrated sharply, Xingxi grew angry, falsely charged him with embezzlement, imprisoned him, and planned to execute him.

sentences.zh: 乃遣珽代行襲為留後。

translations.literal: Taizu then sent Ting to replace Xingxi as acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then sent Ting to replace Feng Xingxi as acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 珽至許州，止傳舍，慰其將吏，行襲病甚，欲使人代受詔，珽曰：「東首加朝服，禮也。

translations.literal: When Ting reached Xu Prefecture, he stopped at the relay station and comforted the commanders and officials. Xingxi was gravely ill and wished to have someone receive the edict in his stead. Ting said: "To face east and put on court dress is the proper rite.
translations.idiomatic: When Ting reached Xu Prefecture, he stopped at the relay station and reassured the commanders and officials. Xingxi was gravely ill and wanted someone to receive the edict for him. Ting said: "To face east in court dress is the proper rite.

sentences.zh: 」乃即臥內見行襲，道太祖語，行襲感泣，解印以授珽。

translations.literal: He then went at once into the sickroom to see Xingxi, conveyed Taizu's words, and Xingxi wept in gratitude and surrendered his seal to Ting.
translations.idiomatic: He went at once into the sickroom, conveyed Taizu's message, and Xingxi wept and surrendered his seal to Ting.

sentences.zh: 珽乃理峻冤，立出之，還報太祖，太祖喜曰：「珽果辦吾事。

translations.literal: Ting then cleared Jun's injustice and released him at once. Returning to report to Taizu, Taizu said with delight: "Ting has indeed handled my business.
translations.idiomatic: Ting cleared Wei Jun's case and released him at once. When he reported back, Taizu said with delight: "Ting has handled my business exactly as I wished.

sentences.zh: 」會歲饑，盜劫汴、宋間，曹州尤甚，太祖復遣珽治之。

translations.literal: Just then famine struck; bandits plundered between Bian and Song, and Cao Prefecture suffered especially. Taizu again sent Ting to deal with it.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck that year. Bandits ravaged the region between Bian and Song, and Cao Prefecture suffered worst of all. Taizu sent Ting back to deal with them.

sentences.zh: 珽至索賊，得大校張彥珂、珽甥李郊等，及牙兵百餘人，悉誅之。

translations.literal: When Ting arrived he hunted down the bandits, seized Senior Commander Zhang Yanke, Ting's nephew Li Jiao, and others, along with more than a hundred guard soldiers, and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Ting arrived he hunted down the bandits, seized Senior Commander Zhang Yanke, his nephew Li Jiao, and more than a hundred guard soldiers, and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 召拜左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Left Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and appointed Left Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 太祖幸河北，至內黃，顧珽曰：「何謂內黃？

translations.literal: Taizu toured Hebei and, reaching Neihuang, turned to Ting and asked: "What does 'Neihuang' mean?
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu toured Hebei and reached Neihuang, he turned to Ting and asked: "What does the name Neihuang mean?

sentences.zh: 」珽曰：「河南有外黃、下黃，故此名內黃。

translations.literal: Ting said: "South of the river there are Waihuang and Xiahuang, hence this place is called Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: Ting said: "South of the river there are Waihuang and Xiahuang, hence this place is called Neihuang—'Inner Huang.'

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「外黃、下黃何在？

translations.literal: Taizu said: "Where are Waihuang and Xiahuang?
translations.idiomatic: Taizu asked: "Where are Waihuang and Xiahuang?

sentences.zh: 」珽曰：「秦有外黃都尉，今在雍丘；

translations.literal: Ting said: "In Qin there was a Commandant of Waihuang; it is now at Yongqiu;
translations.idiomatic: Ting said: "The Qin had a Commandant of Waihuang; it is now at Yongqiu;

sentences.zh: 下黃為北齊所廢，今在陳留。

translations.literal: Xiahuang was abolished by Northern Qi and is now at Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahuang was abolished under Northern Qi and is now at Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 」太祖平生不愛儒者，聞珽語大喜。

translations.literal: Taizu had never in his life cared for Confucian scholars, but hearing Ting's words he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had never cared much for Confucian scholars, but he was greatly pleased by Ting's answer.

sentences.zh: 友珪立，除右散騎常侍，侍講。

translations.literal: When Yougui took the throne, Ting was appointed Right Regular Attendant and Lecturer-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Yougui took the throne, Ting was appointed Right Regular Attendant and Lecturer-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 袁象先討賊，珽為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: When Yuan Xiangxian suppressed the usurper, Ting was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Xiangxian suppressed the usurper, Ting was killed by mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: 琪少舉進士、博學宏辭，累遷殿中侍御史，與其兄珽皆以文章知名。

translations.literal: Qi in his youth passed the jinshi and Erudite Lit. examinations, rose through posts to Palace Censor, and both he and his elder brother Ting were famed for their literary skill.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi passed the jinshi and Erudite Lit. examinations in his youth, rose to Palace Censor, and he and his elder brother Ting were both famed for their literary skill.

sentences.zh: 唐亡，事梁太祖為翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Tang fell, he served Emperor Taizu of Liang as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Tang, he served Emperor Taizu of Liang as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 梁兵征伐四方，所下詔書，皆琪所為，下筆輒得太祖意。

translations.literal: As Liang armies campaigned in every direction, every edict issued was written by Qi; whenever he put pen to paper he captured Taizu's intent.
translations.idiomatic: As Liang armies campaigned across the realm, Qi drafted every edict, and his prose always captured Taizu's intent.

sentences.zh: 末帝時，為御史中丞、尚書左丞，拜同中書門下平章事，與蕭頃同為宰相。

translations.literal: Under the Last Emperor he served as Censor-in-Chief and Left Vice Director of the Chancellery, was appointed Grand Councilor, and served as chief minister alongside Xiao Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Last Emperor he served as Censor-in-Chief and Left Vice Director of the Chancellery, was appointed Grand Councilor, and served alongside Xiao Qing.

sentences.zh: 頃性畏慎周密，琪倜儻負氣，不拘小節，二人多所異同。

translations.literal: Qing was cautious, timid, and meticulous by nature; Qi was free-spirited and proud, unconstrained by small proprieties. The two often differed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Qing was cautious and meticulous by nature; Li Qi was free-spirited and proud, unconstrained by petty proprieties. The two often clashed.

sentences.zh: 琪內結趙巖、張漢傑等為助，以故頃言多沮。

translations.literal: Qi cultivated ties within the court with Zhao Yan, Zhang Hanjie, and others as supporters, and for this reason Qing's proposals were often blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Qi cultivated allies within the court—Zhao Yan, Zhang Hanjie, and others—so Xiao Qing's proposals were often blocked.

sentences.zh: 頃嘗掎摭其過。

translations.literal: Qing once gathered evidence of his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Qing once gathered evidence of his misconduct.

sentences.zh: 琪所私吏當得試官，琪改試為守，為頃所發，末帝大怒，欲竄逐之，而巖等救解，乃得罷為太子少保。

translations.literal: A private clerk of Qi's was due to receive a probationary appointment; Qi changed the probationary appointment to a full one. Qing exposed this. The Last Emperor was furious and wished to exile him, but Yan and the others interceded, and he was merely dismissed to the post of Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: A private clerk of Qi's was due a probationary appointment; Qi changed it to a full appointment. Xiao Qing exposed the abuse. The Last Emperor was furious and wanted to exile him, but Zhao Yan and the others interceded, and Qi was merely demoted to Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗滅梁，得琪，欲以為相，而梁之舊臣多嫉忌之，乃以為太常卿。

translations.literal: When Tang Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and obtained Qi, he wished to make him chief minister, but many former Liang officials were jealous, so he was made Minister of Ceremonies instead.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang destroyed Liang and took Qi into his service, he wished to make him chief minister, but many former Liang officials were jealous, so Qi was appointed Minister of Ceremonies instead.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 同光三年秋，天下大水，京師乏食尤甚，莊宗以朱書御劄詔百僚上封事。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Tongguang, great floods struck the realm; the capital lacked food above all. Zhuangzong issued an imperial letter in vermilion ink summoning the hundred officials to submit sealed memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Tongguang 3, floods ravaged the realm and the capital faced severe food shortages. Zhuangzong issued an imperial letter in vermilion ink summoning officials to submit sealed memorials.

sentences.zh: 琪上書數千言，其說漫然無足取，而莊宗獨稱重之，遂以為國計使。

translations.literal: Qi submitted a memorial of several thousand characters; its proposals were diffuse and worthless, yet Zhuangzong alone praised it highly and appointed him Commissioner for National Finance.
translations.idiomatic: Qi submitted a memorial several thousand characters long. Its proposals were diffuse and worthless, yet Zhuangzong alone praised it and appointed him Commissioner for National Finance.

sentences.zh: 方欲以為相，而莊宗崩。

translations.literal: Just as he was about to be made chief minister, Zhuangzong died.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was about to be made chief minister, Zhuangzong died.

sentences.zh: 明宗入洛陽，群臣勸進，有司具儀，用柩前即位故事。

translations.literal: Mingzong entered Luoyang; the ministers urged him to take the throne, the responsible offices prepared the rites, and the precedent of accession before the coffin was followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong entered Luoyang, the ministers urged him to take the throne. The responsible offices prepared the rites according to the precedent of accession before the coffin.

sentences.zh: 霍彥威、孔循等請改國號，絕土德。

translations.literal: Huo Yanwei, Kong Xun, and others requested that the dynastic name be changed to sever the virtue of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Yanwei, Kong Xun, and others urged that the dynastic name be changed to sever the Li clan's claim to the virtue of Earth.

sentences.zh: 明宗武君，不曉其說，問何謂改號，對曰：「莊宗受唐錫姓為宗屬，繼昭宗以立，而號國曰唐。

translations.literal: Mingzong was a military man and did not understand their argument. He asked what changing the name meant, and they replied: "Zhuangzong received Tang's grant of surname and kinship, succeeded Zhaozong to the throne, and named the state Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was a military man and did not understand their argument. He asked what changing the dynastic name meant. They replied: "Zhuangzong received the Tang imperial surname and kinship status, succeeded Zhaozong, and named the state Tang.

sentences.zh: 今唐天命已絕，宜改號以自新。

translations.literal: Now Tang's Mandate of Heaven is exhausted; the name should be changed to make a fresh start.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Mandate of Tang is exhausted. The dynastic name should be changed to mark a fresh beginning.

sentences.zh: 」明宗疑之，下其事群臣，群臣依違不決。

translations.literal: Mingzong was doubtful and referred the matter to the ministers; the ministers wavered and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was doubtful and referred the matter to the ministers, who wavered and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 琪議曰：「殿下宗室之賢，立功三世，今興兵向闕，以赴難為名，而欲更易統號，使先帝便為路人，則煢然梓宮，何所依往！

translations.literal: Qi argued: "Your Highness is a worthy member of the imperial clan who has rendered service through three reigns. Now you have raised troops toward the capital in the name of rushing to the realm's rescue, yet you wish to change the dynastic title and make the late emperor no more than a stranger—then to whom shall the solitary imperial coffin look for support!
translations.idiomatic: Qi argued: "Your Highness is a worthy member of the imperial clan who has served through three reigns. You marched on the capital in the name of saving the realm, yet to change the dynastic title would make the late emperor a stranger to you—then to whom shall the imperial coffin look for support?

sentences.zh: 」明宗以為然，乃發喪成服，而後即位。

translations.literal: Mingzong thought this right; he then proclaimed mourning, put on mourning garb, and only afterward took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong agreed. He proclaimed mourning, put on mourning garb, and only then took the throne.

sentences.zh: 以琪為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Qi was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 自唐末喪亂，朝廷之禮壞，天子未嘗視朝，而入閣之制亦廢。

translations.literal: Since the disorders at the end of Tang, court ritual had collapsed; the Son of Heaven never held court audiences, and the institution of Entering the Hall was also abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Since the disorders at the end of Tang, court ritual had collapsed. Emperors no longer held regular audiences, and the institution of Entering the Hall was also abandoned.

sentences.zh: 常參之官日至正衙者，傳聞不坐即退，獨大臣奏事，日一見便殿，而侍從內諸司，日再朝而已。

translations.literal: Officials who attended regular court came daily to the main hall; hearing word that the emperor would not sit, they withdrew. Only great ministers reporting business saw him once a day in the side hall, while attendants and inner offices attended twice daily and no more.
translations.idiomatic: Officials due at regular court came daily to the main hall, but hearing that the emperor would not hold audience, they withdrew. Only senior ministers reporting business saw him once a day in the side hall; attendants and inner offices attended twice daily and no more.

sentences.zh: 明宗初即位，乃詔群臣，五日一隨宰相入見內殿，謂之起居。

translations.literal: When Mingzong first took the throne, he decreed that the ministers should follow the chief ministers into the inner hall once every five days, calling this Presentation of Compliments.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong first took the throne, he decreed that ministers should follow the chief ministers into the inner hall once every five days—a practice called Presentation of Compliments.

sentences.zh: 琪以謂非唐故事，請罷五日起居，而復朔望入閣。

translations.literal: Qi held that this was not Tang precedent and requested that the five-day Presentation be abolished and Entering the Hall on the new and full moon be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Qi argued that this was not Tang precedent and asked that the five-day Presentation be abolished and Entering the Hall on the new and full moon be restored.

sentences.zh: 明宗曰：「五日起居，吾思所以數見群臣也，不可罷。

translations.literal: Mingzong said: "The five-day Presentation is my way of seeing the ministers often; it cannot be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong said: "The five-day Presentation is my way of seeing ministers often—it cannot be abolished.

sentences.zh: 而朔望入閣可復。

translations.literal: But Entering the Hall on the new and full moon may be restored.
translations.idiomatic: But Entering the Hall on the new and full moon may be restored.

sentences.zh: 」然唐故事，天子日御殿見群臣，曰常參；

translations.literal: Yet by Tang precedent, when the Son of Heaven daily presided in the hall to see the ministers, it was called regular court attendance;
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang precedent, when the emperor daily presided in the hall to see ministers, it was called regular court attendance;

sentences.zh: 朔望薦食諸陵寢，有思慕之心，不能臨前殿，則禦便殿見群臣，曰入閣。

translations.literal: on the new and full moon, when offerings were made at the imperial tombs and his heart was filled with longing, unable to attend the front hall, he would preside in the side hall to see the ministers—this was called Entering the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: on the new and full moon, when offerings were made at the imperial tombs and the emperor's heart was filled with longing, unable to attend the front hall, he would preside in the side hall to see ministers—this was called Entering the Hall.

sentences.zh: 宣政，前殿也，謂之衙，衙有仗。

translations.literal: Xuanzheng was the front hall, called the Court; the Court had guard formations.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanzheng Hall was the front hall, called the Court; the Court had guard formations.

sentences.zh: 紫宸，便殿也，謂之閣。

translations.literal: Zicheng was the side hall, called the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Zicheng Hall was the side hall, called the Hall.

sentences.zh: 其不御前殿而禦紫宸也，乃自正衙喚仗，由閣門而入，百官俟朝於衙者，因隨以入見，故謂之入閣。

translations.literal: When he did not preside in the front hall but in Zicheng, guard formations were summoned from the main Court and entered through the Hall Gate; officials waiting for court in the Court then followed in to be received, hence it was called Entering the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor did not preside in the front hall but in Zicheng, guard formations were summoned from the main Court and entered through the Hall Gate; officials waiting in the Court then followed in to be received—hence the name Entering the Hall.

sentences.zh: 然衙，朝也，其禮尊；

translations.literal: Yet the Court was formal audience, and its rite was more exalted;
translations.idiomatic: The Court was formal audience, and its rite was more exalted;

sentences.zh: 閣，宴見也，其事殺。

translations.literal: the Hall was a convivial audience, and its ceremony was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: the Hall was an informal audience, and its ceremony was reduced.

sentences.zh: 自乾符已後，因亂禮闕，天子不能日見群臣而見朔望，故正衙常日廢仗，而朔望入閣有仗，其後習見，遂以入閣為重。

translations.literal: From the Qianfu era onward, because disorder had stripped away ritual, the Son of Heaven could not see the ministers daily and saw them only on the new and full moon. Hence on ordinary days guard formations at the main Court were suspended, while Entering the Hall on the new and full moon had formations; afterward this became habitual, and Entering the Hall came to be regarded as the greater ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: From the Qianfu era onward, disorder had stripped away ritual. Emperors could not see ministers daily and saw them only on the new and full moon. Guard formations at the main Court were suspended on ordinary days but retained for Entering the Hall on the new and full moon; over time this became habitual, and Entering the Hall came to be regarded as the greater ceremony.

sentences.zh: 至出御前殿，猶謂之入閣，其後亦廢，至是而復。

translations.literal: Even when he went out to preside in the front hall, it was still called Entering the Hall; afterward that too was abandoned, and now it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the emperor presided in the front hall, the occasion was still called Entering the Hall. That practice too was later abandoned, and now it was restored.

sentences.zh: 然有司不能講正其事。

translations.literal: Yet the responsible offices could not clarify the matter properly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the responsible offices could not clarify the matter properly.

sentences.zh: 凡群臣五日一入見中興殿，便殿也，此入閣之遺制，而謂之起居，朔望一出禦文明殿，前殿也，反謂之入閣，琪皆不能正也。

translations.literal: In general the ministers entered the Zhongxing Hall once every five days—the side hall—a surviving form of Entering the Hall, yet it was called Presentation of Compliments; on the new and full moon they went out once to preside in the Wénming Hall, the front hall, yet that was in turn called Entering the Hall. Qi could correct none of this.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers now entered the Zhongxing Hall—a side hall—once every five days, a surviving form of Entering the Hall, yet it was called Presentation of Compliments. On the new and full moon they attended the Wénming Hall, a front hall, yet that was called Entering the Hall. Qi could correct none of this.

sentences.zh: 琪又建言：「入閤有待制、次對官論事，而內殿起居，一見而退，欲有言者，無由自陳，非所以數見群臣之意也。

translations.literal: Qi further proposed: "Entering the Hall had drafters and secondary responders to discuss affairs, but at Presentation in the inner hall one saw the emperor and withdrew; those who wished to speak had no way to state themselves—this was not the intent of seeing the ministers often.
translations.idiomatic: Qi further proposed: "Entering the Hall allowed drafters and secondary responders to discuss affairs, but at Presentation in the inner hall ministers saw the emperor and withdrew. Those who wished to speak had no way to do so—this defeated the purpose of seeing ministers often.

sentences.zh: 」明宗乃詔起居日有言事者，許出行自陳。

translations.literal: Mingzong then decreed that on Presentation days, those with business to report might step forward and state it themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong then decreed that on Presentation days, officials with business to report might step forward and speak for themselves.

sentences.zh: 又詔百官以次轉對。

translations.literal: He further decreed that the hundred officials should take turns in rotation to respond.
translations.idiomatic: He further decreed that officials should take turns presenting memorials in rotation.

sentences.zh: 是時，樞密使安重誨專權用事，重誨前驅過御史臺門，殿直馬延誤沖之，重誨即臺門斬延而後奏。

translations.literal: At this time the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, An Chonghui, monopolized power. As Chonghui's advance guard passed the Censorate gate, Palace Guard Officer Ma Yan accidentally collided with them. Chonghui had Yan beheaded at the Censorate gate and only then reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At this time An Chonghui, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, monopolized power. As his advance guard passed the Censorate gate, Palace Guard Officer Ma Yan accidentally collided with them. Chonghui had Yan beheaded at the gate and only then reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 琪為中丞，畏重誨不敢彈糾，又懼諫官論列，乃托宰相任圜先白重誨而後糾，然猶依違不敢正言其事。

translations.literal: Qi as Censor-in-Chief feared Chonghui and did not dare impeach him; fearing also that remonstrance officials would criticize him, he had Chief Minister Ren Yuan inform Chonghui first and only then impeach—but still he wavered and did not dare speak plainly of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: As Censor-in-Chief, Qi feared Chonghui and did not dare impeach him. Fearing that remonstrance officials would criticize his inaction, he had Chief Minister Ren Yuan inform Chonghui first and only then lodge an impeachment—but even then he wavered and would not speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 豆盧革等罷相，住圜議欲以琪為相，而孔循、鄭玨沮之，乃止。

translations.literal: When Doulu Ge and others were dismissed as chief ministers, Ren Yuan proposed making Qi chief minister, but Kong Xun and Zheng Jue obstructed it, and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Doulu Ge and others were dismissed as chief ministers, Ren Yuan proposed making Qi chief minister, but Kong Xun and Zheng Jue blocked the appointment.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 琪以狀申中書，言《開元禮》「僕射上事日，中書、門下率百官送上。

translations.literal: Qi submitted a petition to the Secretariat stating that the Kaiyuan Ceremonies say: "On the day a Vice Director assumes office, the Secretariat and Chancellery lead the hundred officials in escorting him to his post."
translations.idiomatic: Qi petitioned the Secretariat, citing the Kaiyuan Ceremonies: "On the day a Vice Director assumes office, the Secretariat and Chancellery lead all officials in escorting him to his post."

sentences.zh: 」中書下太常，禮院言無送上之文，而琪已落新授，復舉上儀，皆不可。

translations.literal: The Secretariat referred it to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the Rites Office said there was no text about escorting to office, and Qi had already received the new appointment and again requested the assumption rite—none of it could be done.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat referred the matter to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. The Rites Office said there was no provision for such an escort, and since Qi had already received the appointment and was again requesting the assumption ceremony, none of it could be granted.

sentences.zh: 明宗討王都，已破定州，自汴還洛，琪當率百官至上東門，而請至偃師奉迎。

translations.literal: Mingzong campaigned against Wang Du, had already taken Ding Prefecture, and was returning from Bian to Luoyang. Qi ought to have led the hundred officials to the Upper East Gate, but instead asked to go as far as Yanshi to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong campaigned against Wang Du, took Ding Prefecture, and returned from Bian to Luoyang, Qi should have led officials to the Upper East Gate—but instead asked to go as far as Yanshi to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 其奏章言「敗契丹之兇黨，破真定之逆城」，坐誤以定州為真定，罰俸一月。

translations.literal: In his memorial he wrote "defeated the Khitan villainous faction and broke the rebel city of Zhending"; he was fined one month's salary for mistakenly calling Ding Prefecture Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial he wrote of "defeating the Khitan villainous faction and breaking the rebel city of Zhending." He was fined one month's salary for mistakenly calling Ding Prefecture Zhending.

sentences.zh: 霍彥威卒，詔琪撰神道碑文。

translations.literal: When Huo Yanwei died, Qi was ordered to compose the tomb inscription.
translations.idiomatic: When Huo Yanwei died, the court ordered Qi to compose his tomb inscription.

sentences.zh: 彥威故梁將，而琪故梁相也，敘彥威在梁事不曰偽，為馮道所駁。

translations.literal: Yanwei had been a Liang general and Qi a Liang chief minister; in recounting Yanwei's service under Liang he did not call it illegitimate, and Feng Dao rebuked him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei had been a Liang general and Qi a Liang chief minister. In recounting Yanwei's service under Liang, Qi did not call the regime illegitimate, and Feng Dao rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 琪為人重然諾，喜稱人善。

translations.literal: Qi as a man valued his promises and liked to praise others' virtues.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was a man who kept his word and liked to praise others' virtues.

sentences.zh: 少以文章知名，亦以此自負。

translations.literal: In youth he was famed for his literary skill and took pride in this as well.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed for his literary skill from youth and took pride in it.

sentences.zh: 既貴，乃刻牙版為金字曰「前鄉貢進士李琪」，常置之坐側。

translations.literal: Once he had risen high, he carved an ivory tablet in gilt characters reading "Former Presented Scholar Li Qi" and always kept it at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had risen high, he carved an ivory tablet in gilt characters reading "Former Presented Scholar Li Qi" and kept it always at his side.

sentences.zh: 為人少持重，不知進退，故數為當時所沮。

translations.literal: As a man he lacked steady judgment and did not know when to advance or withdraw, and for this reason was often obstructed by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: He lacked steady judgment and did not know when to advance or withdraw, and for that reason was often blocked by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 以太子太傅致仕，卒，年六十。

translations.literal: He retired as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent and died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent and died at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 鄭玨，唐宰相綮之諸孫也。

translations.literal: Zheng Jue was a great-grandson of Tang chief minister Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jue was a great-grandson of the Tang chief minister Zheng Qi.

sentences.zh: 其父徽，為河南尹張全義判官。

translations.literal: His father Hui served as aide to Zhang Quanyi, Prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui served as aide to Zhang Quanyi, Prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 玨少依全義居河南，舉進士數不中，全義以玨屬有司，乃得及第。

translations.literal: Jue in youth relied on Quanyi and lived in Henan; he took the jinshi examination several times without passing, until Quanyi recommended him to the authorities and he finally passed.
translations.idiomatic: Jue lived in Henan under Zhang Quanyi's patronage from youth. He failed the jinshi examination several times until Quanyi recommended him to the authorities and he finally passed.

sentences.zh: 昭宗時，為監察御史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Zhaozong he served as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhaozong he served as Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖即位，拜左補闕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizu of Liang took the throne, he was appointed Left Supplementation Official.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu of Liang took the throne, he was appointed Left Supplementation Official.

sentences.zh: 梁諸大臣以全義故數薦之，累拜中書舍人、翰林學士奉旨。

translations.literal: The great ministers of Liang repeatedly recommended him on Quanyi's account, and he rose through posts to Drafting Official in the Secretariat and Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Liang ministers repeatedly recommended him on Zhang Quanyi's account, and he rose to Drafting Official in the Secretariat and Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 末帝時，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Under the Last Emperor he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Last Emperor he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 明宗幸汴州，六軍家屬自洛遷汴，而明宗又欲幸鄴都，軍士愁怨，大臣頗以為言。

translations.literal: Mingzong visited Bianzhou; the families of the Six Armies moved from Luoyang to Bian, and Mingzong also wished to visit Yedu. The soldiers were distressed and resentful, and the great ministers spoke out considerably against it.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong visited Bianzhou, and the families of the Six Armies were moved from Luoyang to Bian. When Mingzong then wished to visit Yedu as well, the soldiers grew distressed and resentful, and the great ministers spoke out strongly against the plan.

sentences.zh: 明宗不省，上下洶洶，轉相動搖，獨玨稱贊，以為當行。

translations.literal: Mingzong did not take heed. Above and below there was uproar, unrest spreading from one to another. Only Jue expressed approval, holding that the journey ought to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong paid no heed. Uproar spread above and below, unrest rippling from rank to rank. Only Jue voiced approval, insisting the journey should go forward.

sentences.zh: 趙鳳極言於安重誨，重誨驚懼，入見明宗切諫，乃詔罷其行。

translations.literal: Zhao Feng spoke forcefully to An Chonghui. Chonghui, alarmed and afraid, entered audience with Mingzong and urgently remonstrated, whereupon an edict canceled the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng spoke forcefully to An Chonghui. Alarmed, Chonghui entered audience with Mingzong and urgently remonstrated, and an edict was issued canceling the journey.

sentences.zh: 而玨又稱贊之，以為宜罷。

translations.literal: Jue again expressed approval, holding that cancellation was proper.
translations.idiomatic: Jue again voiced approval, holding that cancellation was the right course.

sentences.zh: 玨在相位既碌碌無所為，又病聾，孔循罷樞密使，玨不自安，亟以疾求去職。

translations.literal: Jue as chief minister had achieved nothing of note; moreover he suffered from deafness. When Kong Xun was dismissed as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Jue felt ill at ease and urgently pleaded illness to resign.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister Jue had accomplished nothing of note, and he was moreover afflicted with deafness. When Kong Xun was dismissed as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Jue grew uneasy and urgently pleaded illness to resign his post.

sentences.zh: 明宗數留之，玨章四上，乃拜左僕射致仕，賜鄭州莊一區。

translations.literal: Mingzong repeatedly tried to retain him. Jue submitted memorials four times before he was appointed Left Vice Minister and retired, and was granted an estate in Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong repeatedly tried to keep him, but Jue submitted memorials four times before he was appointed Left Vice Minister and retired, and was granted an estate in Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded the title of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously awarded the title of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 李愚，字子晦，渤海無棣人也。

translations.literal: Li Yu, courtesy name Zihui, was a native of Wudi in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, courtesy name Zihui, was a native of Wudi in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 愚為人謹重寡言，好學，為古文。

translations.literal: Yu was by nature cautious, grave, and sparing of speech; he loved learning and wrote in the ancient style.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was by nature cautious and grave, sparing of speech; he loved learning and wrote in the ancient style.

sentences.zh: 滄州節度使盧彥威以愚為安陵主簿，丁母憂解去。

translations.literal: Lu Yanwei, military governor of Cangzhou, appointed Yu Chief Clerk of Anling; he resigned upon entering mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanwei, military governor of Cangzhou, appointed Yu Chief Clerk of Anling; he resigned when he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 後遊關中，劉季述幽昭宗於東內，愚以書說韓建，使圖興復，其言甚壯。

translations.literal: Later he traveled to Guanzhong. Liu Jishu imprisoned Emperor Zhaozong in the Eastern Inner Palace; Yu wrote to Han Jian urging him to plot restoration—the language was stirring indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he traveled to Guanzhong. Liu Jishu had imprisoned Emperor Zhaozong in the Eastern Inner Palace; Yu wrote to Han Jian urging him to plot restoration, and his words were stirring indeed.

sentences.zh: 建不能用，乃去之洛陽。

translations.literal: Han could not employ him, so he went to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Han could not act on his counsel, so Yu went to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 舉進士、宏詞，為河南府參軍。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and hongci examinations and served as aide in the Henan Prefecture office.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and hongci examinations and served as aide in the Henan Prefecture office.

sentences.zh: 白馬之禍，愚復去之山東，與李延光相善，延光以經術事梁末帝為侍講，數稱薦愚，愚由此得召。

translations.literal: After the calamity at Baima, Yu again went east to Shandong. He became friendly with Li Yanguang, who served the Last Emperor of Liang as lecturing attendant on account of his classical learning and repeatedly praised and recommended Yu—by this means Yu received the summons.
translations.idiomatic: After the calamity at Baima, Yu went east again to Shandong. He became friendly with Li Yanguang, who served the Last Emperor of Liang as lecturing attendant on account of his classical learning and repeatedly praised and recommended Yu; by this means Yu received the summons.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜左拾遺、崇政院直學士。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed Left Reminder and Direct Academician of the Chongzheng Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Left Reminder and Direct Academician of the Chongzheng Academy.

sentences.zh: 衡王友諒，末帝兄也，梁大臣李振等皆拜之，獨愚長揖，末帝以責愚曰：「衡王朕拜之，卿獨揖，可乎？

translations.literal: The Prince of Heng, Youliang, was the Last Emperor's elder brother. Li Zhen and other great ministers of Liang all bowed to him; Yu alone gave a deep salute with arms folded. The Last Emperor rebuked Yu, saying: "The Prince of Heng—I bow to him. You alone salute—is that permissible?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Heng, Youliang, was the Last Emperor's elder brother. Li Zhen and the other great ministers of Liang all bowed to him, but Yu alone gave a deep salute with arms folded. The Last Emperor rebuked Yu, saying, "The Prince of Heng—I bow to him. You alone salute—is that permissible?"

sentences.zh: 」愚曰：「陛下以家人禮見之，則拜宜也。

translations.literal: Yu said: "Your Majesty receives him with family courtesy—then bowing is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Your Majesty receives him with family courtesy, so bowing is fitting."

sentences.zh: 臣於王無所私，豈宜妄有所屈？

translations.literal: I have no personal tie to the prince—how should I recklessly bend myself?"
translations.idiomatic: I have no personal tie to the prince—how should I recklessly bend myself?"

sentences.zh: 」坐言事忤旨，罷為鄧州觀察判官。

translations.literal: For this matter of remonstrance that defied the imperial will, he was dismissed and made administrative aide to the military governor of Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For remonstrating in a manner that defied the imperial will, he was dismissed and made administrative aide to the military governor of Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗滅梁，愚朝京師，唐諸公卿素聞愚學古，重之，拜主客郎中、翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong of Tang destroyed Liang, Yu attended court at the capital. Tang officials had long heard of Yu's classical learning and held him in esteem; he was appointed Director of the Bureau of Receptions and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong of Tang destroyed Liang, Yu attended court at the capital. Tang officials had long heard of Yu's classical learning and held him in esteem; he was appointed Director of the Bureau of Receptions and Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 魏王繼岌伐蜀，辟愚都統判官。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wei, Jiji, marched against Shu, he recruited Yu as aide to the overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wei, Jiji, marched against Shu, he recruited Yu as aide to the overall commander.

sentences.zh: 蜀道阻險，議者以謂宜緩師待變而進，招討使郭崇韜以決於愚，愚曰：「王衍荒怠，亂國之政，其人厭之。

translations.literal: The roads into Shu were perilous and obstructed. Those debating the matter said the army ought to advance slowly and wait for changes; the campaign commissioner Guo Chongtao sought Yu's decision. Yu said: "Wang Yan is negligent and dissolute, his rule ruining the state—the people revile him.
translations.idiomatic: The roads into Shu were perilous and obstructed. Those debating the matter said the army ought to advance slowly and wait for changes; campaign commissioner Guo Chongtao sought Yu's decision. Yu said, "Wang Yan is negligent and dissolute, his government ruining the state, and the people revile him.

sentences.zh: 乘其倉卒，擊其無備，其利在速，不可緩也。

translations.literal: Seize their unpreparedness in haste—the advantage lies in speed; we must not delay."
translations.idiomatic: Seize their unpreparedness in haste—strike while they are off guard. The advantage lies in speed; we must not delay."

sentences.zh: 」崇韜以為然，而所至迎降，遂以滅蜀。

translations.literal: Chongtao agreed; wherever they went they were met with surrender, and thus Shu was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao agreed. Wherever they went they were met with surrender, and thus Shu was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 初，軍行至寶雞，招討判官陳乂稱疾請留，愚厲聲曰：「陳乂見利則進，知難則止。

translations.literal: At first, when the army reached Baoji, the campaign aide Chen Yi pleaded illness and asked to remain behind. Yu said in a stern voice: "Chen Yi advances when he sees profit and stops when he knows difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the army reached Baoji, campaign aide Chen Yi pleaded illness and asked to remain behind. Yu said in a stern voice, "Chen Yi advances when he sees profit and stops when he knows difficulty.

sentences.zh: 今大軍涉險，人心易搖，正可斬之以徇。

translations.literal: Now the great army crosses dangerous ground and hearts are easily shaken—this is precisely when he should be beheaded to make an example."
translations.idiomatic: Now the great army crosses dangerous ground and hearts are easily shaken—this is precisely when he should be beheaded to make an example."

sentences.zh: 」由是軍中無敢言留者。

translations.literal: From this, none in the army dared speak of remaining behind.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, none in the army dared speak of remaining behind.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，累遷兵部侍郎承旨。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Yu rose through successive posts to Vice Minister of War and Academician-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, Yu rose through successive posts to Vice Minister of War and Academician-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 明宗祀天南郊，愚為宰相馮道、趙鳳草加恩制，道鄙其辭，罷為太常卿。

translations.literal: When Mingzong performed the southern suburban sacrifice to Heaven, Yu drafted edicts of grace on behalf of chief ministers Feng Dao and Zhao Feng. Dao looked down on the phrasing and had Yu dismissed to serve as Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong performed the southern suburban sacrifice to Heaven, Yu drafted edicts of grace on behalf of chief ministers Feng Dao and Zhao Feng. Dao looked down on the phrasing and had Yu dismissed to serve as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 任圜罷相，乃拜愚中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: When Ren Yuan left the chancellorship, Yu was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren Yuan left the chancellorship, Yu was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 愚為相，不治第宅，借延賓館以居。

translations.literal: As chief minister, Yu built no mansion; he borrowed the Hall for Extending Guests and made it his dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister, Yu built no mansion; he borrowed the Hall for Extending Guests and made it his home.

sentences.zh: 愚有疾，明宗遣宦官視之，見其敗毯敝席，四壁蕭然，明宗嗟嘆，命以供帳物賜之。
