translations.literal: When Yu fell ill, Mingzong sent eunuchs to visit him. They found worn carpets and tattered mats, the four walls utterly bare. Mingzong sighed in admiration and ordered furnishings granted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu fell ill, Mingzong sent eunuchs to visit him. They found worn carpets and tattered mats, the four walls utterly bare. Mingzong sighed in admiration and ordered furnishings granted to him.

sentences.zh: 潞王反，犯京師，湣帝夜出奔。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu rebelled, marched on the capital, and Emperor Min fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu rebelled, marched on the capital, and Emperor Min fled by night.

sentences.zh: 明日，愚與馮道至端門，聞帝已出，而朱弘昭、馮赟皆已死，愚欲至中書候太后進止，道曰：「潞王已處處張榜招安，今即至矣，何可俟太后旨也？

translations.literal: The next day Yu and Feng Dao came to the Gate of Correctness. Hearing that the emperor had already departed and that Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun were both dead, Yu wished to go to the Secretariat and await the empress dowager's decision. Dao said: "The Prince of Lu has already posted placards everywhere offering amnesty—he will arrive at once. How can we wait for the empress dowager's command?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yu and Feng Dao came to the Gate of Correctness. Hearing that the emperor had already departed and that Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun were both dead, Yu wished to go to the Secretariat and await the empress dowager's decision. Dao said, "The Prince of Lu has already posted placards everywhere offering amnesty—he will arrive at once. How can we wait for the empress dowager's command?"

sentences.zh: 」乃相與出迎。

translations.literal: Thereupon they went out together to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they went out together to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 廢帝入立，罷道出鎮同州，以劉句為相。

translations.literal: The deposed emperor entered and took the throne; Dao was dismissed and sent to govern Tong Prefecture, and Liu Xu was made chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor entered and took the throne; Dao was dismissed and sent to govern Tong Prefecture, and Liu Xu was made chief minister.

sentences.zh: 句性褊急，而愚素剛介，動輒違戾。

translations.literal: Xu was by nature narrow and impatient, while Yu had always been upright and unyielding—they clashed at every turn.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was by nature narrow and impatient, while Yu had always been upright and unyielding—they clashed at every turn.

sentences.zh: 句與馮道姻家，愚數以此誚句，兩人遂相誼詬，乃俱罷。

translations.literal: Xu and Feng Dao were related by marriage; Yu repeatedly mocked Xu on this account. The two then traded abuse, and both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Feng Dao were related by marriage, and Yu repeatedly mocked Xu on this account. The two then traded abuse, and both were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 愚守左僕射。

translations.literal: Yu retained the post of Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yu retained the post of Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 是時，兵革方興，天下多事，而愚為相，欲依古以創理，乃請頒《唐六典》示百司，使各舉其職，州縣貢士，作鄉飲酒禮，時以其迂闊不用。

translations.literal: At this time warfare was rising and the realm was beset with troubles. As chief minister, Yu wished to govern anew according to antiquity. He requested that the Tang Six Canon be promulgated to the hundred offices so each might perform its duties, that prefectures and counties present scholars, and that village drinking ceremonies be performed—the age deemed this impractical and did not employ it.
translations.idiomatic: At this time warfare was rising and the realm was beset with troubles. As chief minister, Yu wished to govern anew according to antiquity. He requested that the Tang Six Canon be promulgated to the hundred offices so each might perform its duties, that prefectures and counties present scholars, and that village drinking ceremonies be performed—but the age deemed this impractical and did not adopt it.

sentences.zh: 湣帝即位，有意於治，數召學士，問以時事，而以愚為迂，未嘗有所問。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min took the throne, intent on good government, he repeatedly summoned academicians and questioned them on current affairs—but deeming Yu impractical, he never questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min took the throne, intent on good government, he repeatedly summoned academicians and questioned them on current affairs—but deeming Yu impractical, he never questioned him.

sentences.zh: 廢帝亦謂愚等無所事，常目宰相曰：「此粥飯僧爾！

translations.literal: The deposed emperor also said that Yu and the others had nothing to do, and would often eye the chief ministers and say: "These are merely rice-bowl monks!"
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor also said that Yu and the others had nothing to do, and would often eye the chief ministers and say, "These are merely rice-bowl monks!"

sentences.zh: 」以謂飽食終日，而無所用心也。

translations.literal: Meaning men who eat their fill all day and apply their minds to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: By this he meant men who eat their fill all day and apply their minds to nothing.

sentences.zh: 清泰二年，以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingtai he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qingtai he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 盧導，字熙化，范陽人也。

translations.literal: Lu Dao, courtesy name Xihua, was a native of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dao, courtesy name Xihua, was a native of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 唐末舉進士，為監察御史。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang he passed the jinshi examination and served as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tang he passed the jinshi examination and served as Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 唐亡事梁，累遷左司郎中、侍御史知雜事，以病免。

translations.literal: After Tang fell he served Liang, rising through posts to Director in the Left Department and Supervising Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs; he retired on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After Tang fell he served Liang, rising through posts to Director in the Left Department and Supervising Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs, and retired on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 唐明宗時，召拜右諫議大夫，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Under Tang Mingzong he was summoned and appointed Right Remonstrance and Reviewing Official, then promoted to Drafting Official in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang Mingzong he was summoned and appointed Right Remonstrance and Reviewing Official, then promoted to Drafting Official in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 潞王從珂自鳳翔以兵犯京師，湣帝出奔於衛州。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu, Fromke, marched on the capital from Fengxiang with troops, and Emperor Min fled to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu, Fromke, marched on the capital from Fengxiang with troops, and Emperor Min fled to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 宰相馮道、李愚集百官於天宮寺，將出迎潞王於郊，京師大恐，都人藏竄，百官久而不集，惟導與舍人張昭先至。

translations.literal: Chief ministers Feng Dao and Li Yu gathered the officials at the Temple of the Heavenly Palace, preparing to go out and welcome the Prince of Lu in the suburbs. The capital was greatly alarmed; people hid themselves; officials were long in assembling—only Lu Dao and Drafting Official Zhang Zhao arrived first.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Feng Dao and Li Yu gathered the officials at the Temple of the Heavenly Palace, preparing to go out and welcome the Prince of Lu in the suburbs. The capital was greatly alarmed; people hid themselves; the officials were slow to assemble—only Lu Dao and Drafting Official Zhang Zhao arrived first.

sentences.zh: 馮道請導草箋勸進，導曰：「潞王入朝，郊迎可也，若勸進之事，豈可輕議哉！

translations.literal: Feng Dao asked Lu Dao to draft a memorial urging accession. Lu Dao said: "For the Prince of Lu to enter court, a suburban welcome is fitting—but as for urging accession, how can that be lightly discussed?"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao asked Lu Dao to draft a memorial urging accession. Lu Dao said, "For the Prince of Lu to enter court, a suburban welcome is fitting—but as for urging accession, how can that be lightly discussed?"

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「勸進其可已乎？

translations.literal: Feng Dao said: "Can urging accession be stopped?"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao said, "Can urging accession be stopped?"

sentences.zh: 」導曰：「今天子蒙塵於外，遽以大位勸人，若潞王守節不回，以忠義見責，其將何辭以對？

translations.literal: Lu Dao said: "The Son of Heaven today suffers dust in exile; to hastily offer the great throne to another—if the Prince of Lu holds to his integrity and does not accept, and righteousness and loyalty are demanded of us, with what words shall we answer?"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dao said, "The Son of Heaven today suffers dust in exile; to hastily offer the great throne to another—if the Prince of Lu holds to his integrity and does not accept, and righteousness and loyalty are demanded of us, with what words shall we answer?"

sentences.zh: 且上與潞王，皆太后子也，不如率百官詣宮門，取太后進止。

translations.literal: Moreover, both the emperor and the Prince of Lu are sons of the empress dowager—better to lead the hundred officials to the palace gates and seek the empress dowager's decision."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, both the emperor and the Prince of Lu are sons of the empress dowager—better to lead the hundred officials to the palace gates and seek the empress dowager's decision."

sentences.zh: 」語未終，有報曰：「潞王至矣。

translations.literal: Before he had finished speaking, a report came: "The Prince of Lu has arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Before he had finished speaking, a report came: "The Prince of Lu has arrived."

sentences.zh: 」京城巡檢使安從進催百官班迎，百官紛然而去。

translations.literal: The capital patrol commissioner An Congjin urged the officials to form ranks and welcome him; the officials scattered away in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: The capital patrol commissioner An Congjin urged the officials to form ranks and welcome him, and the officials scattered away in confusion.

sentences.zh: 潞王止於正陽門外，道又促導草箋，導對如初。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu halted outside the Gate of Correct Yang; Feng Dao again pressed Lu Dao to draft the memorial, and Lu Dao answered as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu halted outside the Gate of Correct Yang; Feng Dao again pressed Lu Dao to draft the memorial, and Lu Dao answered as before.

sentences.zh: 李愚曰：「吾輩罪人，盧舍人言是也。

translations.literal: Li Yu said: "We are men guilty of crime—Attendant Lu speaks rightly."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu said, "We are men guilty of crime—Attendant Lu speaks rightly."

sentences.zh: 」導終不草箋。

translations.literal: Lu Dao never drafted the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dao never drafted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 導後事晉為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Later Lu Dao served Jin as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lu Dao served Jin as Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 天福六年卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianfu he died, aged seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 司空颋

translations.literal: Si Kongting
translations.idiomatic: Si Kongting

sentences.zh: 司空颋，貝州清陽人也。

translations.literal: Si Kongting was a native of Qingyang in Bei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Si Kongting was a native of Qingyang in Bei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐僖宗時，舉進士不中，後去為羅紹威掌書記。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xizong of Tang he failed the jinshi examination; later he left to serve Luo Shaowei as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xizong of Tang he failed the jinshi examination; later he left to serve Luo Shaowei as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 紹威卒，入梁為太府少卿。

translations.literal: When Shaowei died, he entered Liang service as Vice Director of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaowei died, he entered Liang service as Vice Director of the Treasury.

sentences.zh: 楊師厚鎮天雄，颋解官往依之。

translations.literal: When Yang Shihou governed Tianxiong, Ting resigned his office and went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Shihou governed Tianxiong, Kongting resigned his office and went to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 師厚卒，賀德倫代之。

translations.literal: When Shihou died, He Delun replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shihou died, He Delun replaced him.

sentences.zh: 張彥之亂，命判官王正言草奏詆斥梁君臣，正言素不能文辭，又為兵刃所迫，流汗浹背，不能下筆。

translations.literal: During Zhang Yan's rebellion, he ordered aide Wang Zhengyan to draft a memorial denouncing the sovereign and ministers of Liang. Wang had never been skilled at literary composition, and was moreover pressed by blades at his back—sweat soaked through to his spine, and he could not set pen to paper.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhang Yan's rebellion, he ordered aide Wang Zhengyan to draft a memorial denouncing the sovereign and ministers of Liang. Wang had never been skilled at literary composition, and was moreover pressed by blades at his back—sweat soaked through to his spine, and he could not set pen to paper.

sentences.zh: 彥怒，推正言下榻，詬曰：「鈍漢辱我！

translations.literal: Yan was enraged, pushed Wang from the couch, and cursed: "You dull-witted oaf—you disgrace me!"
translations.idiomatic: Yan was enraged, pushed Wang from the couch, and cursed, "You dull-witted oaf—you disgrace me!"

sentences.zh: 」顧書吏問誰可草奏者，吏即言颋羅王時書記，乃馳騎召之。

translations.literal: He turned to the clerks and asked who could draft the memorial; a clerk immediately said Ting had been secretary under Prince Luo, and a rider was sent at full gallop to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to the clerks and asked who could draft the memorial; a clerk immediately said Kongting had been secretary under Prince Luo, and a rider was sent at full gallop to summon him.

sentences.zh: 颋為亂兵劫其衣，以敝服蔽形而至，見彥長揖，神氣自若，揮筆成文，而言甚淺鄙，彥以其易曉，甚喜，即給以衣服仆馬，遂以為德倫判官。

translations.literal: Rioters had stripped Ting of his clothes; he came covered in shabby garments, saw Yan with a deep salute, bearing himself with complete composure. He waved his brush and completed the text—the language was crude indeed, but Yan found it easy to understand and was greatly pleased. He was immediately given clothes, servants, and horses, and was made He Delun's aide.
translations.idiomatic: Rioters had stripped Kongting of his clothes; he came covered in shabby garments, saw Yan with a deep salute, and bore himself with complete composure. He waved his brush and completed the text—the language was crude indeed, but Yan found it easy to understand and was greatly pleased. He was immediately given clothes, servants, and horses, and was made He Delun's aide.

sentences.zh: 德倫以魏博降晉，晉王兼領天雄，仍以颋為判官。

translations.literal: When Delun surrendered Weibo to Jin, the Prince of Jin concurrently took command of Tianxiong and still kept Ting as aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Delun surrendered Weibo to Jin, the Prince of Jin concurrently took command of Tianxiong and still kept Kongting as aide.

sentences.zh: 梁、晉相距河上，常以颋權軍府事。

translations.literal: As Liang and Jin faced each other across the Yellow River, Ting was often entrusted with provisional charge of military headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As Liang and Jin faced each other across the Yellow River, Kongting was often entrusted with provisional charge of military headquarters affairs.

sentences.zh: 颋為郭崇韜所惡，崇韜數言其受賂。

translations.literal: Ting was hated by Guo Chongtao, who repeatedly spoke of his taking bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Kongting was hated by Guo Chongtao, who repeatedly spoke of his taking bribes.

sentences.zh: 都虞候張裕多過失，颋屢以法繩之。

translations.literal: Command assistant Zhang Yu had many faults; Ting repeatedly held him to account by law.
translations.idiomatic: Command assistant Zhang Yu had many faults; Kongting repeatedly held him to account by law.

sentences.zh: 颋有侄在梁，遣家奴召之，裕擒其家奴，以謂通書於梁。

translations.literal: Ting had a nephew in Liang and sent a household slave to summon him; Yu seized the slave and claimed he was carrying correspondence to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Kongting had a nephew in Liang and sent a household slave to summon him; Yu seized the slave and claimed he was carrying correspondence to Liang.

sentences.zh: 莊宗族殺之。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong's kinsmen killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong's kinsmen killed him.
